data.narrative:
Proxima Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Francesco Sciortino, Lucio Milanese, Jorrit Lion, Jonathan Schilling, and Martin Kubie. The valuation analysis draws on a frontier-tech sector comprising 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private competitors including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised of €200M as a value proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $2.8B. This method reflects the capital intensity and development trajectory characteristic of frontier nuclear ventures at this stage.

The peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied: while four nuclear energy peers exist in the comp universe, the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables did not yield three or more datapoints. A broader cross-sector median would introduce material noise. Consequently, the analysis rests on the single applicable method, generating a triangulated range of $2.4B (low) to $3.2B (high), with a median of $2.8B. Key uncertainties include the liquidity and exit timeline for frontier nuclear technologies, regulatory pathway clarity, and the sustainability of capital deployment in this sector.
